original_question: Evaluate the suitability of performance-based budgeting for a public health department that allocates funds to vaccination services, using service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and achievement of annual vaccination targets as performance indicators.

transformations.transformed_question: Define performance-based budgeting and identify service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual target achievement as performance indicators.
Explain how linking budget allocations to service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual vaccination targets can connect public expenditure with service performance.
Classify service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual vaccination target achievement according to whether each measures service reach, expenditure efficiency, or target attainment.
Examine how the three stated indicators provide different information about the performance of vaccination services funded by the public health department.
Develop a performance-based budget framework for the vaccination service, linking funding decisions to service coverage, cost per vaccinated person, and annual target achievement.

heading: Example 599: Linguistics — Phonetics: Place and Manner of Articulation
discipline_course_topic: Linguistics — Phonetics: Place and Manner of Articulation
original_question: Classify the English consonant sounds /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/ according to their place and manner of articulation.

transformations.transformed_question: Define place of articulation and manner of articulation in the classification of consonant sounds.
Explain how the location and type of constriction in the vocal tract distinguish the consonant sounds /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/.
Examine the articulatory features of /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/ to distinguish differences in their places and manners of articulation.
Verify whether the classification of /f/ as a bilabial stop and /k/ as a velar stop is consistent with their articulatory characteristics.
Construct a phonetic classification matrix for /p/, /t/, /k/, /f/, and /s/, showing each sound's place and manner of articulation.

heading: Example 600: CSE — Computer Architecture: Cache Write Policies
discipline_course_topic: CSE — Computer Architecture: Cache Write Policies
original_question: Compare write-through and write-back cache policies in terms of when modified data is transferred to main memory, memory traffic, and the handling of modified cache blocks.

transformations.transformed_question: Define write-through and write-back cache policies and identify when each policy transfers modified data to main memory.
Determine when main memory is updated under each policy after a processor modifies a cached data block.
Examine how immediate memory updates in write-through caching and deferred updates in write-back caching affect memory traffic and the management of modified cache blocks.

Assess whether write-back caching is preferable to write-through caching when reducing main-memory traffic is the primary design objective, while accounting for the need to track modified cache blocks.
Develop a comparative cache-write policy model showing the sequence of operations after a processor modifies a cached block under write-through and write-back policies.
